sentences.zh: 《南齊書》，八紀，十一志，四十列傳，合五十九篇，梁蕭子顯撰。

translations.literal: The 《Book of Southern Qi》: eight annals, eleven treatises, forty biographies, fifty-nine fascicles in all, compiled by Xiao Zixian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Southern Qi》 comprises eight annals, eleven treatises, and forty biographies—fifty-nine fascicles in all—written by Xiao Zixian of the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 始江淹已爲十志，沈約又爲《齊紀》，而子顯自表武帝，別爲此書。

translations.literal: At first Jiang Yan had already composed ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》, but Zixian, having himself petitioned Emperor Wu, separately produced this book.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan had already drafted ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》; but Zixian, having presented himself to Emperor Wu of Liang, undertook this work as a separate history.

sentences.zh: 臣等因校正其訛謬，而敘其篇目，曰：

translations.literal: We, your subjects, therefore corrected its errors and blunders, and set forth its table of contents, saying:
translations.idiomatic: We, your subjects, have corrected its errors and set forth the table of contents, saying:

sentences.zh: 將以是非得失、興壞理亂之故而爲法戒，則必得其所託，而後能傳於久，此史之所以作也。

translations.literal: When one intends to take right and wrong, gain and loss, rise and ruin, order and chaos as models and warnings, one must secure the right person as one's medium, and only then can it be transmitted for long—this is why histories are written.
translations.idiomatic: When history is meant to serve as warning and model from the rights and wrongs, gains and losses, rise and ruin, and order and chaos of the past, it must find the right historian to carry it; only then can it endure. That is why histories are written.

sentences.zh: 然而所託不得其人，則或失其意，或亂其實，或析理之不通，或設辭之不善，故雖有殊功韙德非常之迹，將闇而不章，鬱而不發，而檮杌嵬瑣姦回凶慝之形，可幸而掩也。

translations.literal: Yet when the medium is not the right person, then one may lose the intent, or corrupt the facts, or fail to reason through clearly, or compose ineffectively; thus even extraordinary merit and great virtue may grow obscure and fail to shine forth, while the shapes of taowu villains, base petty men, treacherous subversives, and vicious evildoers may fortunately be covered up.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the historian is not the right person, the intent may be lost, the facts distorted, the reasoning muddled, or the style poor; then even extraordinary merit and towering virtue may lie hidden and never break into the light, while villains, petty scoundrels, traitors, and wicked men may by good fortune escape exposure.

sentences.zh: 嘗試論之，古之所謂良史者，其明必足以周萬事之理，其道必足以適天下之用，其智必足以通難知之意，其文必足以發難顯之情，然後其任可得而稱也。

translations.literal: I have tried to discuss this: what the ancients called a fine historian—his clarity must suffice to comprehend all principles of things, his Way must suffice to serve the needs of the world, his wisdom must suffice to penetrate what is hard to know, and his style must suffice to express what is hard to reveal; only then can his task be held to have been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Consider what the ancients meant by a fine historian: his clarity must encompass the principles of all things; his Way must meet the needs of the world; his wisdom must penetrate what is hard to know; his prose must express what is hard to make plain—only then can his work be said to have fulfilled its charge.

sentences.zh: 何以知其然邪？

translations.literal: How do we know this to be so?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know that this is so?

sentences.zh: 昔者，唐虞有神明之性，有微妙之德，使由之者不能知，知之者不能名。

translations.literal: In former times, Tang and Yu possessed a divine nature and subtle virtue, such that those who followed them could not understand it, and those who understood could not name it.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Tang and Yu possessed a divine nature and subtle virtue: those who followed them could not fully grasp it, and those who grasped it could not put it into words.

sentences.zh: 以爲治天下之本，號令之所布，法度之所設，其言至約，其體至備，以爲冶天下之具。

translations.literal: They took this as the root of governing the world; in what they proclaimed as commands and established as laws and institutions, their words were supremely concise and their forms supremely complete—it was treated as the toolkit for governing the world.
translations.idiomatic: They made this the foundation of governing the realm: in the commands they issued and the laws and institutions they established, their words were supremely spare and their forms supremely complete—the whole apparatus for ruling the world.

sentences.zh: 而爲二《典》者，推而明之，所記者，豈獨其迹邪？

translations.literal: Yet those who composed the two 《Canons》 developed and clarified this: what they recorded—was it only their traces?
translations.idiomatic: Those who composed the two 《Canons》 of Yao and Shun developed and clarified this: what they recorded—was it only their outward deeds?

sentences.zh: 並與其深微之意而傳之。

translations.literal: They also transmitted along with them their profound and subtle intentions.
translations.idiomatic: They transmitted their profound and subtle intentions as well.

sentences.zh: 小大精粗，無不盡也；

translations.literal: Whether great or small, fine or coarse, nothing was left incomplete;
translations.idiomatic: Great and small, fine and coarse—nothing was left out;

sentences.zh: 本末先後，無不白也。

translations.literal: whether root or branch, earlier or later, nothing was left unclear.
translations.idiomatic: root and branch, earlier and later—nothing was left obscure.

sentences.zh: 使誦其說者，如出乎其時；

translations.literal: so that those who recited their account might feel as if they had stepped forth from that very age;
translations.idiomatic: So that those who read their account might feel as though they had stepped out of that very age;

sentences.zh: 求其指者，如即乎其人。

translations.literal: and those who sought their meaning might feel as if they were face to face with the men themselves.
translations.idiomatic: and those who sought their meaning might feel as though they stood face to face with the men themselves.

sentences.zh: 是可不謂明足以周萬事之理，道足以適天下之用，智足以通難知之意，文足以發難顯之情者乎？

translations.literal: Can this not be called clarity sufficient to encompass all principles, a Way sufficient to serve the world's needs, wisdom sufficient to penetrate what is hard to know, and style sufficient to express what is hard to reveal?
translations.idiomatic: Can this not be called clarity that encompasses all principles, a Way that serves the world's needs, wisdom that penetrates what is hard to know, and prose that expresses what is hard to make plain?

sentences.zh: 則方是之時，豈特任政者皆天下之士哉？

translations.literal: Then at the time when these texts existed, was it only those charged with government who were men of talent under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: At the time when such texts existed, was it only those who held office who ranked among the talented men of the realm?

sentences.zh: 蓋執簡操筆而隨者，亦皆聖人之徒也。

translations.literal: Roughly speaking, even those who took up bamboo strips and wielded the brush in their wake were all disciples of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who took up the brush and followed in their wake were disciples of the sages.

sentences.zh: 兩漢以來爲史者，去之遠矣。

translations.literal: Since the Two Han dynasties, those who wrote histories have stood far from this standard.
translations.idiomatic: Historians since the Two Han have fallen far short of this standard.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷從五帝三王旣歿數千載之後，秦火之餘，因散絕殘脫之經，以及傳記百家之說，區區掇拾，以集著其善惡之迹，興廢之端，又創己意以爲本紀、世家、八書、列傳之文，斯亦可謂奇矣。

translations.literal: Sima Qian, thousands of years after the Five Emperors and Three Kings had passed away and in the aftermath of the Qin burning, relying on scattered and broken classics and on the reports and traditions of the hundred schools, gathered them bit by bit to compile records of good and evil deeds and the beginnings of rise and fall, and further devised his own scheme for the Annals, Hereditary Houses, Eight Treatises, and Biographies—this may indeed be called remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian, thousands of years after the Five Emperors and Three Kings had died and in the wreckage left by the Qin burning of the books, pieced together what survived of broken classics and the writings of the hundred schools, gathered bit by bit the traces of good and evil and the beginnings of rise and fall, and then invented his own structure of Annals, Hereditary Houses, Eight Treatises, and Biographies—this was indeed a marvel.

sentences.zh: 然而蔽害天下之聖法，是非顛倒而採摭謬亂者，亦豈少哉！

translations.literal: Yet how many things did he obscure and harm of the sage laws of the world, how many right and wrong judgments did he overturn in gathering and selecting what was mistaken and confused!
translations.idiomatic: Yet how often did he obscure the sage laws of the realm, invert right and wrong, and gather up what was mistaken and confused!

sentences.zh: 是豈可不謂明不足以周萬事之理，道不足以適天下之用，智不足以通難知之意，文不足以發難顯之情者乎？

translations.literal: Can this not be said to be clarity insufficient to encompass all principles, a Way insufficient to serve the world's needs, wisdom insufficient to penetrate what is hard to know, and style insufficient to express what is hard to reveal?
translations.idiomatic: Can he not be said to lack clarity enough to encompass all principles, a Way enough to serve the world's needs, wisdom enough to penetrate what is hard to know, and prose enough to express what is hard to make plain?

sentences.zh: 夫自三代以後爲史者如遷之文，亦不可不謂儁偉拔出之材、非常之士也，然顧以謂明不足以周萬事之理，道不足以適天下之用，智不足以通難知之意，文不足以發難顯之情者，何哉？

translations.literal: Among historians after the Three Dynasties, for work like Qian's one cannot but call him a towering talent and extraordinary man—yet why should one say that his clarity, Way, wisdom, and style fall short of the standard just named?
translations.idiomatic: Among historians after the Three Dynasties, a writer like Qian cannot but be called a towering talent and an extraordinary man—yet why say that his clarity, Way, wisdom, and prose still fall short?

sentences.zh: 蓋聖賢之高致，遷固有不能純達其情而見之於後者矣，故不得而與之也。

translations.literal: It is that the lofty reach of sages and worthies—Qian inherently could not fully convey their sentiments and present them to posterity, and so could not be classed with them.
translations.idiomatic: The lofty reach of the sages and worthies—Qian could not wholly convey their inner truth and set it before posterity; therefore he cannot be ranked with the finest historians of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 遷之得失如此，況其他邪？

translations.literal: If Qian's merits and faults were such, how much more so others?
translations.idiomatic: If Qian's strengths and failings were such, what of the rest?

sentences.zh: 至於宋、齊、梁、陳、後魏、後周之書，蓋無以議爲也。

translations.literal: As for the books of Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Wei, and Later Zhou, there is scarcely anything worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: As for the histories of Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Wei, and Later Zhou, there is scarcely anything worth discussing at all.

sentences.zh: 子顯之於斯文，喜自馳騁，其更改破析刻彫藻繢之變尤多，而其文益下，豈夫材固不可以強而有邪？

translations.literal: In this writing Zixian delighted in following his own fancy; his alterations, splitting apart, carving, and ornamental elaborations were especially many, yet his prose grew ever poorer—can talent really not be forced into existence?
translations.idiomatic: In this work Zixian delighted in riding his own whim; his revisions, splittings, carvings, and ornamental flourishes were especially numerous, yet his prose grew ever weaker—can a talent truly be forced into being?

sentences.zh: 數世之史旣然，故其事迹曖味，雖有隨世以就功名之君，相與合謀之臣，未有赫然得傾動天下之耳目，播天下之口者也。

translations.literal: When histories of several generations are thus, their deeds grow dim: even rulers who rode with the times to win fame and ministers who plotted together have none who could plainly stir the eyes and ears of the world and claim the mouths of the world.
translations.idiomatic: When histories of several generations are like this, their deeds grow dim: even rulers who rode the times to fame and ministers who plotted together fail to stir the eyes and ears of the world or seize the tongues of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 而一時偷奪傾危悖理反義之人，亦幸而不暴著於世，豈非所託不得其人故邪？

translations.literal: Yet men of that time who stole thrones, overturned states, defied reason and righteousness also fortunately failed to be exposed to the world—is this not because they did not find the right historian as medium?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile men of the age who stole power, overturned states, and defied reason and righteousness also escape exposure—is this not because they did not find the right historian to carry their record?

sentences.zh: 可不惜哉！

translations.literal: Is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 蓋史者所以明夫治天下之道也，故爲之者亦必天下之材，然後其任可得而稱也。

translations.literal: For history is what clarifies the Way of governing the world; therefore its author must likewise be a man of talent under Heaven, and only then can the task be held to have been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: History exists to clarify the Way of governing the realm; its author must therefore be a man of talent fit for the world, and only then can the charge be said to have been met.

sentences.zh: 豈可忽哉！

translations.literal: How could one neglect this!
translations.idiomatic: How could one neglect this!

sentences.zh: 豈可忽哉！

translations.literal: How could one neglect this!
translations.idiomatic: How could one neglect this!

sentences.zh: 臣恂、臣寶臣、臣穆、臣藻、臣洙、臣覺、臣彥若、臣鞏謹敘目錄昧死上。

translations.literal: Your subjects Xun, Baochen, Mu, Zao, Zhu, Jue, Yanruo, and Gong respectfully present this catalogue and report it at the risk of death.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects Xun, Baochen, Mu, Zao, Zhu, Jue, Yanruo, and Gong respectfully present this catalogue and submit it at the risk of our lives.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
